Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints consistent with cervical whiplash,
including neck pain, stiffness, and headache. The reported injury is well matched to the mechanism and force of the crash. Over a
total of 7 visits, care followed a typical course of conservative management, consisting of manual therapy, guided
range-of-motion exercises, and home stretching instructions. Visit frequnecy was reduced steadily as symptoms improved and the
patient returned to normal daily activities. Examination findings include reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle
tenderness that support the reported injury, while other neurological and orthopedic tests were within normal limits. No prior
injury to the cervical spine or surrounding soft tissue is known from the patient's history. Bliling records reflect one charge per
service with no duplicated or repeated entries. The patient was dsicharged with instructions to continue home exercises and return
if symptoms recur.
